title: The upcoming stock market collapse (& how to prepare for it)
creator: Akshat Shrivastava
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: A macro risk-management lesson, not a stock pitch. Akshat opens by showing how consensus 'experts' were wrong on de-dollarization (2024) and the AI-bubble call (early 2026) — the lesson being that experts don't do your risk management for you. On India, Nifty weekly candles show a head-and-shoulders breakdown; whether the 22,000 support holds with volume decides if the ~18,800-19,000 zone comes into play, with 18,500-19,000 his next buy zone. Fundamental risks he lists: no AI-growth engine, a still-rich 21x forward PE, high oil and energy prices, weak monsoons, and a 2.5-year zero-return consolidation (-5% in USD terms). On the US, QQQ sits at all-time highs but he doesn't call valuations stretched — the risk is an earnings slowdown as GDP projections trend down (2.2% for 2026 to 2.1% 2027 to 1.9% 2028) alongside rising inflation, i.e. stagflation; a 10-20% correction 'can happen any day'. Investor advice: SIP investors run an 80/20 invest/cash split and slow fresh deploys until clarity; 100% US investors trim to ~75% and rotate 25% into alternatives (gold, developed markets — explicitly not India); pure India investors go large-cap heavy with ~20% gold as a currency-risk hedge, and never add mid/small caps against this momentum. No explicit calls in this one — no BUY/SELL/HOLD on any ticker.
